placements.why: The envelope's entire content is a database/analytics-pipeline migration decision (PostgreSQL to QuantumDB) with its performance/cost rationale and timeline — a technical-infrastructure category. No strata exists yet in this repo, and nothing in the empty structure is even close, so this is a NEW top-level mint rather than an EXACT or INSPIRED match. Architecture is the natural home for both narrative leaves minted below.
placements.title: technical system and infrastructure decisions get their own organizational home
placements.frame: what technical/infrastructure decision-making — its authority, its justification, its scheduling — belongs in this envelope's contribution?

placements.title: a migration decision hardens from spoken choice into scheduled, authoritative record
placements.frame: what marks a database or infrastructure migration as authoritatively settled and scheduled, whether spoken aloud or fixed in the written record?
placements.why: src-1's spoken 'We're switching from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB' performs a decisive first-person-plural commitment; src-3's arrow-notation summary re-records that same commitment as settled fact; src-5's fixed 'Q3 2026' timeline pins it to a schedule. Across relational and conviction reads these register as authority-ranking, operational-commitment acts (matching the MigrationDecisionAuthority position grouping) rather than mere description — this is a recurring subject (how technical decisions get enacted and scheduled) future envelopes can keep feeding, not a one-time fact, so it clears the narrative grain test. No existing leaf covers this in the empty graph, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Architecture strata (INSPIRED-adjacent to that category, though standing as its own theme).

placements.title: technical migration choices are justified by quantified performance and cost gains rather than by fiat
placements.frame: what quantitative performance or cost grounds are offered to justify a technical/infrastructure migration decision?
placements.why: src-2's spoken '10x query performance, lower licensing cost' and src-4's written restatement '10x analytical queries' both cast the migration's justification in proportional cost-benefit terms (market-pricing per the relational read; 'claim' rather than 'decision' per conviction) — this is the recurring pattern of justifying technical choices with metrics, a subject beyond this single 10x figure that future engineering-decision envelopes will keep feeding, not a bare fact to fold into the commitment leaf above (per the grain-test rule, the metric itself is evidence for this justification theme, not its own leaf). Kept distinct from Narrative_InfrastructureMigrationCommitment because it tracks the grounds offered, not the act of deciding, mirroring the MigrationPerformanceJustification position split.
